projects.title: Multi-Tenant SaaS Platform
projects.tagline: One deployment. Eight enterprise clients. Zero data leakage.
projects.description: A Spring Boot 3 backend serving 8 enterprise clients from a single deployment, with per-tenant data isolation enforced at the database layer via PostgreSQL row-level security — not application code.
projects.problem: The client was running 8 separate deployments of the same application — one per enterprise customer. Every bug fix required 8 deployments. Every schema migration ran 8 times. Infrastructure costs were scaling linearly with clients instead of logarithmically.
projects.approach: Designed a shared-schema multi-tenancy model using PostgreSQL row-level security policies. Each API request sets a session-level tenant context variable; RLS policies filter all queries automatically. Spring Boot's filter chain injects the tenant ID from the JWT before any repository call. Zero application-layer tenant checks needed.
projects.outcome: Reduced infrastructure cost by 65%. Deployment time dropped from 4 hours (8 sequential deploys) to 18 minutes (1 deploy). Onboarding a new enterprise client went from 3 weeks of DevOps work to a 4-minute database operation.

projects.title: LLM Document Processing Pipeline
projects.tagline: GPT-4o + Spring Batch. 70% less manual review.
projects.description: An AI-assisted pipeline that ingests unstructured legal and financial documents, extracts structured data using OpenAI function calling, validates against business rules, and routes exceptions to human reviewers — all orchestrated by Spring Batch.
projects.problem: A legal services firm was spending 40 hours/week manually extracting data from contracts and financial statements. The documents were inconsistently formatted, came from 12 different sources, and had to be cross-referenced against a compliance database before any downstream processing.
projects.approach: Built a Spring Batch pipeline with three phases: (1) document ingestion and normalisation via Apache Tika, (2) structured extraction using GPT-4o function calling with a strict JSON schema, (3) rule-based validation with confidence scoring. Documents below a confidence threshold are routed to a human review queue. Embeddings stored in pgvector enable semantic deduplication.
projects.outcome: Manual review time dropped by 70%. The pipeline processes 500+ documents per day with 94% straight-through rate. The remaining 6% that reach human review are genuinely ambiguous — not false positives from a brittle regex.

projects.title: Real-Time Logistics Tracking
projects.tagline: 50,000 shipment events per day. Sub-200ms p99.
projects.description: A Kafka-backed event streaming platform for real-time shipment tracking across a logistics network of 200+ vehicles. Event sourcing for the order lifecycle enables full audit trails and replay capability.
projects.problem: The existing system polled a GPS database every 30 seconds per vehicle. With 200+ vehicles, that was 400+ queries per minute on a single PostgreSQL instance that was already struggling. Location updates were 30–90 seconds stale. A major enterprise client was threatening to leave over SLA violations.
projects.approach: Replaced polling with a Kafka event stream. GPS devices publish location events to a partitioned topic (partitioned by vehicle ID for ordering guarantees). Spring Boot consumers maintain materialised state in Redis for sub-millisecond reads. PostgreSQL receives only persisted state changes, not every event. Event sourcing on the order aggregate enables full replay for debugging and compliance.
projects.outcome: Location staleness dropped from 30–90s to under 3s. Database load reduced by 85%. The enterprise client renewed their contract. p99 API latency for location queries: 180ms.

projects.title: Payroll Compliance Engine
projects.description: A configurable payroll calculation engine handling Indian statutory compliance across 6 states — EPFO, ESIC, TDS, PT — for 12 enterprise clients. Replaced a brittle Excel-based process that had caused two payroll errors in the previous year.
projects.problem: Payroll was calculated in Excel by a team of 4 accountants. The spreadsheets had grown to 15,000 rows with circular references and undocumented macros. Two calculation errors in 12 months had resulted in incorrect salaries for 340 employees and significant reputational damage with enterprise clients.
projects.approach: Modelled each statutory rule as a composable, testable Java function. A rule engine evaluates applicable rules per employee based on state, salary band, and employment type. Spring Batch processes the full payroll run in parallel chunks. Each calculation step is logged with inputs and outputs for full auditability. Integration with EPFO/ESIC/TDS APIs via a resilient adapter with retry and circuit breaker.
projects.outcome: Zero payroll errors since deployment. Month-end batch processing time: 45 minutes (down from 6 hours manual). New client onboarding: 4 days (down from 3 weeks). The system has processed ₹40 Cr+ monthly without a single statutory compliance failure.

projects.title: Payment Reconciliation Engine
projects.description: A transaction reconciliation system matching 100,000+ daily payment records across 3 payment gateways. Idempotency keys and distributed locking eliminated duplicate charge incidents. Built as the sole backend engineer on a 12-person fintech startup.
projects.problem: The startup was manually reconciling payment records in spreadsheets every morning. Duplicate charges had occurred twice, costing ₹2L in refunds and damaging trust with early enterprise clients. The manual process took 3 hours daily and was error-prone under time pressure.
projects.approach: Built a reconciliation engine that fetches settlement reports from 3 gateway APIs, normalises them to a canonical format, and matches against internal transaction records using a multi-pass algorithm (exact match → fuzzy match → exception queue). Idempotency keys on all payment operations prevent duplicate processing. Redis distributed locks prevent race conditions during concurrent reconciliation runs.
projects.outcome: 99.97% reconciliation accuracy on first pass. Zero duplicate charge incidents since deployment. Daily reconciliation time: 8 minutes automated vs 3 hours manual. The system caught a gateway-side duplicate charge bug that would have cost ₹4L before it was noticed.

faq.question: Are you currently available for new projects?
faq.answer: Yes — I am currently available for new engagements. I typically take on 1–2 projects at a time to ensure full focus. If your timeline is flexible, reach out early to reserve a slot.

faq.question: Do you work remotely?
faq.answer: Yes, fully remote. I am based in India (UTC+5:30) and have worked with clients across Europe, the US, and Southeast Asia. I schedule overlap hours to match your team's working day.

faq.question: What engagement models do you offer?
faq.answer: Fixed-price projects for well-scoped work, hourly for audits and reviews, retainer for ongoing support, and consulting for architecture and advisory. Most greenfield builds are fixed-price after a scoping call.

faq.question: How long does a typical project take?
faq.answer: A backend API takes 2–8 weeks. A full-stack product build is 4–16 weeks. Enterprise multi-tenant platforms run 8–24 weeks. Duration depends on scope, not padding — I scope honestly before committing.

faq.question: What is your primary tech stack?
faq.answer: Backend: Java 21 + Spring Boot 3. Frontend: Vue 3 + TypeScript. Database: PostgreSQL. Cloud: AWS (ECS, RDS, Lambda). CI/CD: Jenkins + Docker. I also work with Kafka, Redis, and OpenAI API for AI-assisted systems.

faq.question: Can you work on an existing codebase?
faq.answer: Yes. I regularly join projects mid-flight — rescuing systems that have outgrown their original design, adding features to legacy codebases, or improving performance. I always start with a codebase audit before touching anything.

faq.question: Do you sign NDAs and assign IP?
faq.answer: Yes to both. All client work is covered by a mutual NDA and full IP assignment. You own everything built during the engagement. I retain no rights to your code, data, or business logic.

faq.question: How do you communicate during a project?
faq.answer: Async-first via Slack or email for daily updates. Weekly video calls for progress reviews. I write clear status updates so you always know where things stand — no chasing required.

faq.question: What AI/LLM experience do you have?
faq.answer: I have built production LLM pipelines using OpenAI function calling + Spring Batch, reducing manual document review by 70%. I work with GPT-4o, embeddings, pgvector semantic search, and confidence-scored human review queues.

faq.question: How do I start a project with you?
faq.answer: Send an email or book a 30-minute call via Calendly. We discuss your requirements, I ask clarifying questions, and within 48 hours I send a written scope, timeline, and fixed price. No obligation until you sign.
